title: Code of use by-law amended to ban harassment
subtitle: Also: automated speed enforcement centre, housing funding, intimate partner violence epidemic declaration, Cambridge encampment concerns, advisory committee appointments.
overview: Regional Council amended its Code of Use by-law to prohibit harassing and discriminatory behaviour on Regional premises, including transit. The change adds socio-economic and housing status to the protected grounds, states that lawful protest is not limited, and recognizes the Charter as paramount {{vote:m9}}. Council also asked staff to report on how by-law officers will be trained and what enforcement will look like. Two further amendments were defeated: removing the words "objectionable" and "unwelcome" {{vote:m10}}, and requiring an outside legal peer review {{vote:m11}}.

Council also approved a Region-run processing centre for automated speed enforcement in school zones, subject to 2024 budget approval {{vote:m6}}. It declared intimate partner violence an epidemic, approved housing investment plans and paramedic service enhancements {{vote:m8}}, and settled an expropriation claim in Kitchener and appointed members to four advisory committees {{vote:m12}}.

The meeting ran long because of many delegations. Several residents also spoke about the closure of the 150 Main Street encampment in Cambridge and evictions from Soper Park. That topic was not on the agenda, and no motion was made on it.

decisions.item: Code of Use by-law harassment amendment
decisions.detail: Council amended By-law 13-050 to prohibit harassing or discriminatory behaviour on Regional premises, adding socio-economic and housing status, a lawful-protest protection and a statement that the Charter is paramount {{vote:m9}}.

Council approved a Region of Waterloo processing centre for speed camera infractions in all school zones, with staffing and budget to be brought forward in the 2024 budget and an amended equipment agreement with Redflex {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Housing funding, paramedics and intimate partner violence
decisions.detail: Council approved the COCHI and OPHI housing investment plans with two new staff positions, the 2024 paramedic service enhancements, and a declaration that intimate partner violence is an epidemic, asking the Province to do the same {{vote:m8}}.

Council approved the Scheifele Bridge replacement design, named the Director of Water and Wastewater Services as owner representative for drinking water systems, and allowed administrative penalties for parking on Regional roads {{vote:m5}}.
Council authorized the Regional Solicitor to buy the Kitchener property for $801,000, subject to the solicitor's satisfaction with terms {{vote:m7}}.

decisions.item: Ottawa Street settlement and committee appointments
decisions.detail: Council approved a $743,785 expropriation settlement for 707 Ottawa Street South, raised the Ottawa Street project budget by $215,000, and appointed members to four advisory committees {{vote:m12}}.

debate: Delegates opposed to the by-law said it limits free expression more than necessary. They said the Criminal Code already covers hate speech, that harassment defined by how someone feels is subjective, and that by-law officers should not have to decide such questions.

Delegates in favour described harassment and slurs in public spaces and on transit, including at a recent rally. They said the by-law gives the Region a tool to address it and noted that Edmonton and Calgary have similar by-laws and still see protests. Several delegates welcomed adding housing and socio-economic status.

Staff said harassment is judged by a reasonable-person standard, that the by-law does not apply to Regional roads but does cover facilities and transit, and that no external legal opinion was sought. One councillor asked for an outside peer review, and others said in-house legal staff were sufficient.

Council removed the wording about feeling "tormented, troubled, worried" and the words "causing or permitting". It added the lawful-protest and Charter language. A proposal to delete "objectionable" and "unwelcome" was defeated, with some councillors saying those words mirror human rights and workplace safety law.

Delegates on homelessness said evictions in Cambridge leave people with nowhere legal to shelter, and asked the Region to designate a place to tent. A question from one councillor raised the pressure on other levels of government for funding and safety concerns at 150 Main Street.
